mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a single month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs eroding equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a given month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in >70% of post-trigger windows, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for ≥2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations.
regime_hint: Elevated unemployment and weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of such regimes, or PAYEMS does not show a downward trend during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) above their 12-month moving averages by at least 2% in the same quarter is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust economic momentum supporting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_12mo_avg AND GDPC1 > GDPC1_12mo_avg, both by ≥2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >40% of such events, or RSAFS does not show a corresponding upward spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 3% in a month coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening supply-side constraints and potential future contractionary policy responses.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -3% in a given month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >80% of such months, or CPIAUCSL does not show a corresponding decline.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for two consecutive months during a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 105), the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as expectations of prolonged low rates support equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 105 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such windows, or FEDFUNDS rises above 1% in any subsequent month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above 140,000 in a month triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market resilience that often precedes equity market strength.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of such events, or UNRATE does not decline in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both HOUST and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 4% in the same month are associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening demand signals that pressure earnings growth forecasts.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > -4% AND RSAFS falls > -4% in a given month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of such months, or GDPC1 does not show a decline.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month consecutive decline in INDPRO of at least 1% while UNRATE remains below 4% signals persistent supply-side softness without labor market compensation, leading to a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -1% for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4% during both
regime_hint: Persistent supply weakness without labor offset
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of such windows, or CPIAUCSL shows a compensatory upward trend.
